title: Roulette Router: confidence protocol, lightweight hedging, and operational fallback spec
creator: Asha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This ticket drafts an operational specification for a new lightweight 'Roulette Router' used by the serving runtime to do low-overhead speculative decode routing. The Roulette Router is intended to: (1) pick a candidate model/kernel pair probabilistically based on expected unit cost and acceptance probability, (2) emit concise acceptance signals during prefill/early decode, and (3) provide clear hedging and fallback contracts so downstream layers can gracefully degrade without long tail latency spikes.

Motivation & background:
- Many of our existing playbooks use deterministic prioritization (fastest-first or cheapest-first) but observed brittle behavior under bursty loads and when kernel performance is variable across sequence length distributions.
- Previous speculative routing efforts relied on expensive prefill probes or multi-stage proposals that add scheduling overhead. We need a middle ground: a low-latency probabilistic selector that leverages kernel fingerprints, small prefill samplers, and an acceptance metric that's cheap to compute and robust to noise.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a runtime policy that reduces 95th/99th token-latency tail by enabling early hedging without doubling compute cost in steady state.
  - Surface a compact acceptance signal (0..1) per candidate with clear semantics for callers (e.g., console/rollouts and decode orchestrator).
  - Be kernel-aware: include kernel cost, sequence-length sensitivity, and KV-cache hit heuristics in routing weight computation.
- Non-goals:
  - This ticket does not replace full statistical prefilling experiments or our full multi-probe router. It is a lower-cost routing contract to be used in fast paths and as a complement to heavier probes.

Design overview (high level):
1) Roulette selection weights:
   - Weight(candidate) = softmax( log_accept_prior + log_capacity_factor - beta * estimated_token_cost )
   - log_accept_prior is computed from an exponential moving average (EMA) of historical acceptance_rate for that model/kernel shard on similar request buckets (prompt length, token type).
   - log_capacity_factor is a short-window signal (10s) representing current utilization of the pool.
   - estimated_token_cost includes kernel-specific per-token latency, quantization penalty, and memory-copy overhead.
   - beta is a tunable that trades cost vs acceptance (default 0.8).
   - Roulette sampling: draw k candidates (k configurable, default 1 for cheap path, 2 for hedging path).

2) Acceptance protocol (compact signal):
   - Each candidate emits an acceptance tuple encoded as three small fields: acceptance_score (float string 0..1), token_confidence_delta (float string), and stage ("prefill"|"early_decode").
   - Acceptance semantics: score represents the probability that candidate will produce the same top-k tokens as the top-ranked candidate within the next n tokens. This is calibrated offline and continuously updated by telemetry.
   - Quick interpretation for orchestrator: score >= 0.85 => safe commit; 0.5-0.85 => monitor + potential hedging; <0.5 => fallback immediately.

3) Kernel-aware prefill sampler and micro-probes:
   - Instead of full-prefill probes, use a micro-probe of length 1-3 tokens executed on an opportunistic compute slot to measure kernel latency and early acceptance slope.
   - Micro-probes are probabilistically sampled: p = min(0.2, 0.02 + 0.15 * uncertainty), where uncertainty is derived from EMA variance of acceptance_score.
   - If micro-probe indicates acceptance rise (token_confidence_delta > threshold), promote candidate; otherwise demote.

4) Fallback / hedging contract:
   - Fast-path: single candidate chosen; if acceptance_score falls below 0.5 during early_decode, trigger soft-hedge -> dispatch second candidate (costly) only for remaining tokens, with KV-cache warmup policy described below.
   - Soft-hedge budget: bounded by per-request hedging_budget_tokens (default 32 tokens) and per-customer hedging_quota per minute (safely limits cost spikes).
   - Graceful downgrade: if bandwidth constrained, choose a compressed/quantized variant or lower-context-length candidate. The orchestrator must have an ordered fallback set for each model family.

5) KV-cache & warmup contract:
   - When hedging to a different model/kernel, warmup is limited: the runtime will replay up to warmup_prefix_tokens (default 32) of last context into the new model in a background, throttled fashion while streaming best-effort tokens from first candidate. This reduces quality regressions when switching mid-generation.

Acceptance metrics and telemetry (what we measure):
- Acceptance calibration curve: P(agreement | acceptance_score) aggregated per model/kernel and per prompt bucket.
- Latency impact: delta p50/p95/p99 token-level latency before/after hedging for routed requests.
- Cost impact: hedging_rate (% requests with hedging), average extra tokens generated during hedges, and hedging cost per 100k requests.
- Quality regressions: automated eval on representative prompt sets to detect content divergence when fallback path is used more than X%.
- Model churn signal: rate of acceptance_score drops correlated with model version or kernel updates.

Rollout & safety plan:
- Phase 1: Simulation only (2 weeks) with telemetry flags enabled. Roulette picks simulated but not enacted. Collect acceptance calibration and hedging cost projections.
- Phase 2: Canary (1%) with hedging disabled but router chooses candidates; acceptance_score emitted to orchestrator for monitoring.
- Phase 3: Limited hedging (5%) with per-customer hedging caps and kill-switch feature flag. Monitor cost and latency.
- Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% if telemetry stable and cost within target.

Operational runbooks / playbooks (short):
- SRE: if hedging_cost > threshold or 99th latency regresses, flip roulette.beta=0 (cost-sensitive mode) or disable hedging flag.
- Product/PM: track quality regression dashboard; if top-k divergence > 2% on critical prompts, pause rollouts.

Trade-offs discussed and decisions made:
- Chosen probabilistic sampling over deterministic top-K to avoid pathological lock-in when kernels fluctuate during bursts. Decision rationale: smaller steady-state cost increase for larger tail latency reduction.
- Micro-probes chosen instead of full prefill probes because they provide early slope info at much lower cost; downside is noisier signals — mitigated via EMA and variance-based sampling.
- Acceptance_score calibrated to agreement metric rather than raw logprob to better reflect downstream quality for top-k heavy use cases.

Implementation tasks (owner(s), checklist):
- [ ] Router core: implement Weight(candidate) computation and roulette sampling (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Acceptance signal contract API between runtime and orchestrator (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Micro-probe executor with cheap scheduling hook (owner: Priya Menon)
- [ ] KV-cache warmup gated replay mechanism (owner: Daniel Cho)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards: acceptance calibration curve, hedging cost, quality drift per-model (owner: DataEng: Omar Salazar)
- [ ] Simulation harness and synthetic workloads for validation (owner: QA: Linh Nguyen)

Progress notes / timeline: 
- 2026-02-20: Draft created and shared with Decode & Runtime teams. (this ticket)
- 2026-02-24: Sync with Kernel team — agreed to expose kernel fingerprint and per-token-cost estimate via /metrics API (action: ENG-76219).
- 2026-02-28: Prototype roulette weight function implemented in local branch (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/3009). Early sims show 18% p99 token latency reduction on synthetic short-seq workload with hedging_budget_tokens=16.
- 2026-03-03: Design review feedback from PM (Rajiv Patel): ask to add hedging budget per-tenant; added to spec.
- 2026-03-05: SRE concerns: hedging bursts causing quota exhaustion on Dedicated clusters. Action: add per-pool capacity_factor to weight.
- 2026-03-08: Telemetry schema proposed: acceptance_score as float tag + token_confidence_delta as numeric metric. DataEng to implement. (ticket created: ENG-926001)
- 2026-03-10: Canary plan drafted; flags: roulette.enable (bool), roulette.hedging_pct (0-100), roulette.beta (float), roulette.k_microprobe (int).

Open questions / risks / follow-ups:
- Calibration stability: how often does acceptance calibration need to be refreshed for each model version? (Action: offline experiment with model churn sim).
- Interaction with batching: roulette decisions must respect batching/packing; need pack-aware cost model to avoid cross-request unfairness. (Action: add packing factor to cost estimate).
- Edge-case: long-context requests where KV warmup cost negates hedging gains. Consider per-request override to disable hedging for large context sizes.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- Simulation telemetry for at least 3 representative workloads with hedging cost < 10% overhead and p99 latency improvement >= 10% for the synthetic short-seq workload.
- Router integrated in runtime tests with feature flags and basic hedging flow validated in staging.
- Dashboards available for acceptance calibration and hedging cost.
- Runbook entries added for SRE and PM response actions.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/roulette-router-spec
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/3009
- Simulation harness repo: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/infra/decoding-sims/tree/roulette-experiments
- Telemetry schema ticket: ENG-926001

Reviewers requested: Priya Menon (Runtime), Daniel Cho (Kernel), Omar Salazar (DataEng), Rajiv Patel (PM), SRE on-call.

Notes for future iterations:
- Explore a Bayesian bandit variant (Thompson sampling) if calibration variance remains high; would require slightly heavier per-candidate bookkeeping but may improve long-term convergence.
- Consider exposing per-tenant cost/quality tradeoff knobs in Console (for enterprise customers wanting predictable economic behavior).
